ideas.hypothesis: Moving bus operating subsidies from direct award to competitive tendering lowers subsidy per vehicle-km without reducing reliability or patronage, and the savings are larger where the incumbent was a protected state-owned monopoly.

sources.role: setting/mechanism: Irish 2009 Act retaining direct-award subsidies and entry restrictions; the forgone tendering option
measure: economic value of bus operating subsidy and concessionary reimbursement
setting: operating subsidies to state-owned bus operators and reform in Chinese cities
setting: closed Greek market with monopolistic public operators, a contrast case

ideas.test: Route-level data for Dublin bus routes moved from direct award to a tendered operator (from 2018) and comparable retained routes, about 2015-2019: operating cost or subsidy per vehicle-km, punctuality, and boardings from National Transport Authority reports. Run a difference-in-differences. Replicate with English local authority tendered vs commercial services if data allow.
ideas.disconfirming: Tendered routes show no fall in cost per vehicle-km, or show cost savings accompanied by declining reliability or ridership.

ideas.hypothesis: Integrated intermodal fare products (such as combined Park&Ride plus transit tickets) raise net revenue per passenger. They attract car users and lower fare evasion at interchanges, where evasion is concentrated among transferring passengers facing complex fare structures.

sources.role: setting/mechanism: smart Park&Ride with mode-choice information to shift drivers to rail
method: procedure for introducing new ticket types to raise attractiveness and income
measure: perceived quality factors at urban interchanges from satisfaction surveys
finding/measure: fare evasion and ticket forgery as threats to operator revenue

ideas.test: Operator data from one transit authority that introduced an integrated P&R/transit ticket: monthly ticket revenue, P&R occupancy, and ticket-inspection evasion rates at interchange vs non-interchange stops, 2 years before and after. Run a difference-in-differences, plus a short survey of transferring passengers on fare complexity.
ideas.disconfirming: Evasion at interchanges does not fall relative to other stops, and net revenue per passenger does not rise after integration.

ideas.hypothesis: Network redesigns that add forced transfers (hub-and-spoke) reduce ridership more than standard generalized-cost models predict among commuters who value their in-vehicle time positively, because transfers break up usable travel time. Wellington's 2018 bus network redesign is the test case.

sources.role: mechanism: network planning principles (connective, transfer-based networks) for New Zealand cities
measure: public transport connectivity measures computed for Wellington, Auckland and Christchurch CBDs
mechanism/measure: survey evidence that some Auckland and Wellington commuters value travel time and do not wish to reduce it

ideas.test: Wellington Metlink smartcard boardings by stop pair before and after the July 2018 redesign. Classify origin-destination pairs as newly requiring a transfer or unchanged, and compute connectivity scores. Compare observed ridership change with predictions from a generalized-cost elasticity model. Add a short online survey of affected commuters on positive travel-time value.
ideas.disconfirming: Ridership losses on newly transferring pairs match generalized-cost predictions and do not differ by commuters' positive valuation of travel time.

ideas.hypothesis: Adopting Complete Streets policy raises both cycling and transit commute shares (complements rather than substitutes), with transit gains concentrated where new cycling facilities connect to rail or bus rapid transit stations.

sources.role: setting/method: diffusion of Complete Streets policy and comparison of commute modes across adopting and non-adopting states
mechanism: non-motorized transport as part of an intermodal chain
measure: indicators of urban public transport quality affecting modal split
setting: declining local public transport where supporting policy and infrastructure are lacking

ideas.test: US cities' ACS 5-year commute mode shares, 2005-2019, with Complete Streets adoption dates (National Complete Streets Coalition). Run a staggered difference-in-differences (Callaway-Sant'Anna) for bicycle and transit shares, heterogeneous by the share of transit stations with bike lanes within 1 km (OpenStreetMap).
ideas.disconfirming: Complete Streets adoption raises cycling but lowers or leaves unchanged transit share, even near connected stations.

ideas.hypothesis: Where formal public transport is sparse, motorcycle taxis reduce transport exclusion for women by enabling market and service trips. Bans or restrictions on motorcycle taxis therefore increase forgone trips and travel time more for women than for men.

sources.role: finding: about half of rural motorcycle taxi passengers are women, rising on market days; all operators are male
method: gendered survey of informal transport travel time and delay
setting: role of motorcycle taxis among informal modes and local regulation
mechanism: multi-layered physical and social barriers produce gendered transport exclusion

ideas.test: In a city that restricted motorcycle taxis (e.g., Lagos in 2020) and a comparable unrestricted city, run a repeated household travel-diary survey (or use existing travel surveys) before and after. Estimate a difference-in-differences by gender for trip counts, forgone trips, and travel time to markets and health facilities.
ideas.disconfirming: The restriction changes women's and men's trip rates and travel times equally, or not at all.

ideas.hypothesis: Future-city policies that push cars out of city centres widen the public-transport accessibility gap between segregated peripheral neighbourhoods and the rest of the city, unless they come with frequency increases on routes serving those neighbourhoods.

sources.role: mechanism: 2025 city scenario with growing segregation and car exclusion from centres
finding/mechanism: ethnic segregation and poor public transport produce transport exclusion
method: combined GPS and qualitative methods to trace mobility in excluded areas
measure: travel time and delay by social group

ideas.test: For a city that introduced a car-restricted central zone, compute job accessibility by public transport (GTFS feeds before and after) for each census tract. Measure the change in accessibility gap between high-segregation tracts (dissimilarity or isolation index) and others. Compare cities that did and did not add peripheral frequency.
ideas.disconfirming: The accessibility gap does not widen after car restrictions, even where peripheral service was not increased.

ideas.hypothesis: Low-income fringe households with poor public transport access (forced car ownership) cut non-work social and leisure trips more sharply than other households when fuel prices spike, linking transport affordability stress to social exclusion.

sources.role: measure/setting: forced car ownership among low-income households in Melbourne's fringe
mechanism: links between transport poverty, distributional impacts and social exclusion

ideas.test: Melbourne household travel survey (VISTA) waves or HILDA panel, covering the 2008 fuel price spike. Classify households as forced car owners (low income, car-owning, low PT accessibility). Estimate a difference-in-differences of non-work trip rates and social participation measures before and after the spike, compared with other households.
ideas.disconfirming: Forced car owners reduce social trips no more than other households after fuel price increases.

ideas.hypothesis: Sydney bus contract regions that moved to performance-based contracts with patronage-linked incentives grew patronage per service-km faster than regions that stayed under government operation or fixed gross-cost contracts.

sources.role: mechanism: performance-based bus contracts with patronage growth incentive payments
method: comparative analysis of how state political reform paths shaped public transport in two Australian cities
setting: partial privatization and tendering with service-growth objectives (Genoa)
method: comparative Victoria-NSW regulatory analysis via an investigative panel

ideas.test: Transport for NSW open data on boardings and service kilometres by bus contract region, 2010-2019, with contract-change dates (e.g., outsourcing of former State Transit regions from 2018). Run a staggered difference-in-differences of patronage per service-km, controlling for population and employment growth.
ideas.disconfirming: Patronage per service-km does not grow faster after the move to performance-based contracts relative to unchanged regions.

ideas.hypothesis: Fare-free formal bus service on a corridor draws riders from jeepneys mainly among low-income and off-peak riders, but ridership gains depend more on higher frequency than on the zero fare, and jeepney drivers' daily income falls.

sources.role: finding/method: fare reduction combined with supply improvement analysed via counts and passenger interviews
setting: jeepneys and other informal modes alongside formal transport and local government institutions
measure: passenger preferences over waiting time, frequency, comfort and safety among competing modes

ideas.test: On a Philippine corridor with a free bus program and a comparable control corridor, collect jeepney passenger counts by time of day and driver income diaries before and after launch. Add an intercept survey of free-bus riders on previous mode, income, and the importance of fare versus waiting time.
ideas.disconfirming: Jeepney ridership and driver income on the treated corridor do not fall relative to control, or the diversion is unrelated to rider income and time of day.

ideas.hypothesis: Tricycles serve as first/last-mile feeders, so making trunk public transport free or cheaper increases tricycle trips at feeder terminals (complementarity) rather than reducing them.

sources.role: finding: fare reduction and better supply raised public transport use
setting: tricycles' feeder role within the local informal public transport system
setting/measure: tricycles among available modes and passenger travel patterns on a small island

ideas.test: In a Philippine municipality launching free or reduced-fare trunk service, run tricycle trip counts at terminals near trunk stops and at control terminals far from them, 3 months before and after. Add a short survey of tricycle passengers on onward trunk use.
ideas.disconfirming: Tricycle trips at feeder terminals fall or stay flat relative to control terminals after the fare change.
